## Objectives
* One consolidated, parameterized script for all 8 segments (replaces the per-segment Rmds).
* Each segment tree carries 6 gheatmap columns: Genoflu cluster, Genoflu genotype,
  Genin cluster, Genin genotype, TC cluster, TC genotype.
* The 3 genome-wide genotype scales (genoflu_geno, genin_geno, tc_geno) share ONE master
  palette across all segments, persisted to `palettes/genotype_palettes.rds` so colors are
  stable across segments and reruns. The 3 cluster scales are per-segment (IDs not comparable
  across segments) and get their own seeded palettes.
* Legends are ordered by tip position (top to bottom of the tree), capped to the top-16 most
  frequent values per scale.
* Genin has no HA cluster (`genin_clusterHA` does not exist) so HA's genin-cluster column
  renders all-grey but the slot is kept for layout consistency.
* HA gets an extra variant with an H5 clade column (leftmost); NA gets one with subtype.
* Per segment: full tree + B3.13 + D1.1 genotype-MRCA subtrees.

## helpers
```{r}
# Tip labels ordered top to bottom of a ggtree plot (highest y first).
tip_top_order<-function(ggt){
  ggt$data %>% filter(isTip) %>% arrange(desc(y)) %>% pull(label)
}

# Legend breaks: keep the top-n categories by frequency, then order them by first
# appearance from the top of the tree. vals is a named character vector (names = tips).
# Returns character(0) when everything is NA so the scale's legend shows nothing.
ordered_breaks<-function(vals, tip_order, n = 16){
  present<-vals[!is.na(vals)]
  if(length(present)==0) return(character(0))
  counts<-sort(table(present), decreasing = TRUE)
  keep<-names(counts)[seq_len(min(n, length(counts)))]
  ordered_vals<-vals[tip_order]
  first_seen<-unique(ordered_vals[!is.na(ordered_vals)])
  first_seen[first_seen %in% keep]
}
```

## Master palettes (persisted, shared across segments)
```{r}
palette.file<-"palettes/genotype_palettes.rds"

# Clean the sentinel "unassigned" strings to NA before assigning colors.
clean_vals<-function(x){
  x<-as.character(x)
  x[x %in% c("Not assigned","[unassigned]","")]<-NA
  sort(unique(na.omit(x)))
}

# NA (neuraminidase) type from a subtype string: "H5N1" -> "N1" (NA if no Nx present).
na_type_of<-function(x) str_extract(as.character(x), "N\\d+")

# Build a qualitative palette: shuffle (seeded) so neighboring categories get distinct
# colors, then ramp the brewer palette across them.
make_palette<-function(vals, brewer.name, brewer.n, seed = 42){
  if(length(vals)==0) return(setNames(character(0), character(0)))
  set.seed(seed)
  ord<-sample(vals)
  setNames(colorRampPalette(brewer.pal(brewer.n, brewer.name))(length(ord)), ord)
}

# Build once from the full metadata (all genome-wide values), then persist. Set force=TRUE
# to regenerate intentionally (e.g. after new genotypes enter the data).
build_master_palettes<-function(geno, force = TRUE){
  if(file.exists(palette.file) && !force) return(readRDS(palette.file))
  pals<-list(
    genoflu_geno   = make_palette(clean_vals(geno$genoflu_geno),  "Paired",  12),
    genin_geno     = make_palette(clean_vals(geno$genin_geno),    "Dark2",   8),
    tc_geno        = make_palette(clean_vals(geno$tc_geno),       "Accent",  8),
    subtype_filled = make_palette(clean_vals(geno$subtype_filled),"Pastel2", 8),
    na_type        = make_palette(clean_vals(na_type_of(geno$subtype_filled)),"Pastel2", 8),
    HAclade_filled = make_palette(clean_vals(geno$HAclade_filled),"Pastel1", 9)
  )
  if(!dir.exists("palettes")){dir.create("palettes")}
  saveRDS(pals, palette.file)
  pals
}

#switch to force=F if you don't want to regenerate palette evert time
palettes<-build_master_palettes(geno, force = TRUE)
```

## Per-segment annotation builder
```{r}
build_anno<-function(focal.segment, geno){
  tree.in<-list.files(tree.fold, pattern = paste0("_", focal.segment, "_"), full.names = TRUE)
  tree<-ape::read.tree(tree.in)

  genolook.in<-paste0(genolook.fold, "trim_nodup_nuc_", focal.segment, "_rooted_resid.csv")
  genolook<-read.csv(genolook.in)  # columns: sample, seq_new (already segment-specific)

  tc_col<-paste0("tc_cluster", focal.segment)
  geno_col<-paste0("genoflu_cluster", focal.segment)
  genin_col<-paste0("genin_cluster", focal.segment)  # absent for HA
  have_genin<-genin_col %in% names(geno)

  sel<-geno %>%
    select(sample, taxa2, region,
           all_of(tc_col), all_of(geno_col), any_of(genin_col),
           subtype_filled, HAclade_filled,
           tc_geno, genoflu_geno, genin_geno)

  anno<-data.frame(seq_new = tree$tip.label) %>%
    left_join(genolook %>% select(seq_new, sample), by = "seq_new") %>%
    left_join(sel, by = "sample") %>%
    rename(tc_cluster = all_of(tc_col), geno_cluster = all_of(geno_col))

  if(have_genin){
    anno<-anno %>% rename(genin_cluster = all_of(genin_col))
  } else {
    anno$genin_cluster<-NA_character_
  }

  # Sentinel unassigned -> NA
  anno$genoflu_geno[anno$genoflu_geno=="Not assigned"]<-NA
  anno$genin_geno[anno$genin_geno=="[unassigned]"]<-NA
  anno$genin_cluster[anno$genin_cluster %in% c("[unassigned]","")]<-NA

  # NA type (Nx) derived from the subtype, e.g. H5N1 -> N1 (for the NA-segment plots)
  anno$na_type<-na_type_of(anno$subtype_filled)

  cat("== ", focal.segment, " ==\n", sep="")
  cat("Tips:", length(tree$tip.label),
      "| missing sample:", sum(is.na(anno$sample)),
      "| missing genin_cluster:", sum(is.na(anno$genin_cluster)), "\n")

  list(tree = tree, anno = anno)
}
```

## Per-segment cluster palettes (not shared across segments)
```{r}
build_cluster_palettes<-function(anno, seed = 69){
  list(
    genoflu_cluster = make_palette(clean_vals(anno$geno_cluster),  "Set1", 9, seed),
    genin_cluster   = make_palette(clean_vals(anno$genin_cluster), "Set2", 8, seed),
    tc_cluster      = make_palette(clean_vals(anno$tc_cluster),    "Set3", 12, seed)
  )
}
```

## Column spec builders
```{r}
# A "spec" is one gheatmap column: which anno column, its label, legend name, palette,
# legend cap, and legend columns. make_plot() stacks them left to right.
base_specs<-function(palettes, cl_pals){
  list(
    list(col="geno_cluster",  label="Genoflu cluster",  name="Genoflu cluster",          cols=cl_pals$genoflu_cluster, cap=16, ncol=2),
    list(col="genoflu_geno",  label="Genoflu genotype", name="Genoflu genotype (top16)", cols=palettes$genoflu_geno,   cap=16, ncol=2),
    list(col="genin_cluster", label="Genin cluster",    name="Genin cluster",            cols=cl_pals$genin_cluster,   cap=16, ncol=2),
    list(col="genin_geno",    label="Genin genotype",   name="Genin genotype (top16)",   cols=palettes$genin_geno,     cap=16, ncol=2),
    list(col="tc_cluster",    label="TC cluster",       name="TC cluster (top16)",       cols=cl_pals$tc_cluster,      cap=16, ncol=2),
    list(col="tc_geno",       label="TC genotype",      name="TC genotype (top16)",      cols=palettes$tc_geno,        cap=16, ncol=1)
  )
}

clade_spec<-function(palettes){
  list(col="HAclade_filled", label="H5 clade", name="H5 clade (top16)", cols=palettes$HAclade_filled, cap=16, ncol=2)
}
subtype_spec<-function(palettes){
  list(col="na_type", label="NA type", name="NA type", cols=palettes$na_type, cap=16, ncol=2)
}
```

## Generic plotter
```{r}
# Stack a list of column specs onto a tree. Legend breaks are recomputed from whatever
# tips are in `tree`, so the same function serves full trees and subtrees.
make_plot<-function(tree, anno, specs, file, width = 11, height = 18,
                    font.size = 4, colnames_offset_y = 1.5, legend.box.spacing = 2,
                    legend.key.cm = 0.8, legend.text.size = 14, legend.title.size = 16,
                    legend.title.face = "plain",
                    seg.label = NULL, seg.label.size = 11, seg.label.yfrac = 1.06,
                    n.label.size = 5, n.label.yfrac = 1.02, label.xfrac = 0.05,
                    treescale.fontsize = 3, treescale.gap.frac = NULL,
                    treescale.width = NULL, treescale.right = FALSE, treescale.xfrac = 0.6,
                    left.margin = 34, bottom.margin = 28){
  col_width<-0.10
  gap<-0.01
  NN<-Ntip(tree)
  x_range<-max(node.depth.edgelength(tree))

  # treescale.gap.frac -> gap between scale bar and its label, as a fraction of Ntip.
  # treescale.right -> right-align the bar at the right edge of the tree (rel x = 1),
  # else place its left end at x_range * treescale.xfrac.
  ts.gap<-if(is.null(treescale.gap.frac)) NULL else NN * treescale.gap.frac
  ts.x<-if(isTRUE(treescale.right)){
    x_range - (if(is.null(treescale.width)) 0 else treescale.width)
  } else x_range * treescale.xfrac
  t<-ggtree(tree) +
    geom_treescale(x = ts.x, y = NN, width = treescale.width, fontsize = treescale.fontsize,
                   linesize = 0.5, offset.label = ts.gap)
  tip_order<-tip_top_order(t)

  p<-t
  for(i in seq_along(specs)){
    s<-specs[[i]]
    offset<-x_range * (i*gap + (i-1)*col_width)

    heat<-anno %>%
      column_to_rownames("seq_new") %>%
      select(all_of(s$col)) %>%
      mutate(across(everything(), as.character))
    heat<-heat[rownames(heat) %in% tree$tip.label, , drop = FALSE]

    vals<-setNames(heat[[1]], rownames(heat))
    brks<-ordered_breaks(vals, tip_order, n = s$cap)

    p<-gheatmap(p, heat,
                offset = offset, width = col_width, color = NA,
                colnames = TRUE, colnames_offset_y = colnames_offset_y, hjust = 0,
                font.size = font.size, colnames_position = "top", colnames_angle = 45,
                custom_column_labels = s$label) +
      scale_fill_manual(values = s$cols, na.value = "grey90", name = s$name,
                        breaks = brks, guide = guide_legend(order = i, ncol = s$ncol))

    if(i==1){
      p<-p +
        theme(margins = margin(1,1,1,1,unit = "pt")) +
        coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, NN*1.1), clip = "off")
    }
    if(i<length(specs)){
      p<-p + new_scale_fill()
    }
  }

  # segment name (large bold) + tip count, upper-left
  if(!is.null(seg.label)){
    p<-p +
      annotate("text", x = x_range*label.xfrac, y = NN*seg.label.yfrac, label = seg.label,
               hjust = 0.5, vjust = 1, fontface = "bold", size = seg.label.size) +
      annotate("text", x = x_range*label.xfrac, y = NN*n.label.yfrac, label = paste0("n=", NN),
               hjust = 0.5, vjust = 1, size = n.label.size)
  }

  p_themed<-p + theme(legend.box.spacing = unit(legend.box.spacing, "cm"),
                      legend.key.size = unit(legend.key.cm, "cm"),
                      legend.text = element_text(size = legend.text.size),
                      legend.title = element_text(size = legend.title.size, face = legend.title.face),
                      plot.margin = margin(5.5, 5.5, bottom.margin, left.margin, "pt"))
  # file = NULL -> don't write, just return the themed object (used to assemble composites)
  if(!is.null(file)){
    ggsave(file, plot = p_themed, width = width, height = height, units = "in")
  }
  invisible(p_themed)
}

# Extract the clade rooted at the MRCA of tips with anno[[filter_col]] == filter_val,
# then plot it with the same specs.
plot_subtree<-function(tree, anno, specs, filter_col, filter_val, file, seg.label = NULL,
                       font.size = 5, colnames_offset_y = 1, ...){
  tips<-anno$seq_new[which(anno[[filter_col]]==filter_val)]
  tips<-tips[tips %in% tree$tip.label]
  cat("Tips in", filter_val, ":", length(tips), "\n")
  if(length(tips)<3){message("  too few tips, skipping ", filter_val); return(invisible(NULL))}
  node<-getMRCA(tree, tip = tips)
  sub<-ape::extract.clade(tree, node)
  cat("  subtree tips:", Ntip(sub), "\n")
  make_plot(sub, anno, specs, file = file,
            width = 11, height = 18, font.size = font.size, colnames_offset_y = colnames_offset_y,
            seg.label = seg.label, ...)
}
```

# Run all segments
```{r}
# top-8 most common genotypes (data-driven), used for genotype-MRCA subtrees
top_genotypes<-function(x, n = 8){
  x<-as.character(x); x[x %in% c("Not assigned","[unassigned]","")]<-NA
  na.omit(names(sort(table(x), decreasing = TRUE))[seq_len(n)])
}
genoflu_top<-top_genotypes(geno$genoflu_geno)
genin_top<-top_genotypes(geno$genin_geno)
safe<-function(s) gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9._-]", "_", s)
cat("GenoFLU subtrees:", paste(genoflu_top, collapse=", "), "\n")
cat("GenIn subtrees:", paste(genin_top, collapse=", "), "\n")

# genotype subtrees go in genotype_trees/<scheme>_<genotype>/ (one subfolder per genotype)
gt.out<-paste0(f.out, "genotype_trees/")
if(!dir.exists(gt.out)){dir.create(gt.out)}
geno_dir<-function(prefix, g){
  d<-paste0(gt.out, prefix, "_", safe(g), "/")
  if(!dir.exists(d)){dir.create(d)}
  d
}

for(seg in segments){
  bundle<-build_anno(seg, geno)
  tree<-bundle$tree
  anno<-bundle$anno

  cl_pals<-build_cluster_palettes(anno)
  specs<-base_specs(palettes, cl_pals)
  # genoflu-genotype subtrees drop the genin columns; genin-genotype subtrees drop genoflu
  specs_genoflu<-Filter(function(s) !s$col %in% c("genin_cluster","genin_geno"), specs)
  specs_genin  <-Filter(function(s) !s$col %in% c("geno_cluster","genoflu_geno"), specs)

  # full tree, 6 columns (slightly smaller legend tiles)
  make_plot(tree, anno, specs,
            file = paste0(f.out, seg, "_full_gheatmap.tiff"),
            seg.label = seg, legend.key.cm = 0.65)

  # GenoFLU genotype-MRCA subtrees (4 cols: genoflu cluster/geno + TC cluster/geno)
  for(g in genoflu_top){
    plot_subtree(tree, anno, specs_genoflu, "genoflu_geno", g,
                 file = paste0(geno_dir("genoflu", g), seg, "_genoflu_", safe(g), "_gheatmap.tiff"),
                 seg.label = seg)
  }
  # GenIn genotype-MRCA subtrees (4 cols: genin cluster/geno + TC cluster/geno)
  for(g in genin_top){
    plot_subtree(tree, anno, specs_genin, "genin_geno", g,
                 file = paste0(geno_dir("genin", g), seg, "_genin_", safe(g), "_gheatmap.tiff"),
                 seg.label = seg)
  }

  # HA/NA variant with an extra leftmost column
  if(seg=="HA"){
    specs_v<-c(list(clade_spec(palettes)), specs)
    make_plot(tree, anno, specs_v,
              file = paste0(f.out, seg, "_full_gheatmap_H5clade.tiff"),
              width = 12, seg.label = seg, legend.key.cm = 0.65)
  }
  if(seg=="NA"){
    specs_v<-c(list(subtype_spec(palettes)), specs)
    make_plot(tree, anno, specs_v,
              file = paste0(f.out, seg, "_full_gheatmap_subtype.tiff"),
              width = 12, seg.label = seg, legend.key.cm = 0.65)
  }
}
```

# Publication composites (cowplot)
Assembles 2x2 grids for insertion into a Word doc. Two segment groups:
group A = PB2, PB1, PA, HA; group B = NA, NP, NS, M. Built for the full trees and
for every GenoFLU/GenIn top-8 genotype (genotype composites land in each genotype's
folder as `composite_plot_geno_<group>.tiff`). Exported as TIFF at 300 dpi.

This chunk is self-contained: it rebuilds each panel object with the same functions
used above (`make_plot(..., file = NULL)` returns the themed panel without writing the
per-segment file), so it can be run on its own. It re-renders the trees, so it is
compute-heavy — expect a long run for the full trees.
```{r}
library(cowplot)

# segment groups (2x2 each), in panel order
comp_groups<-list(
  "PB2_PB1_PA_HA" = c("PB2","PB1","PA","HA"),
  "NA_NP_NS_M"    = c("NA","NP","NS","M")
)

# export dims for a 2x2 grid of tall tree+legend panels; LZW keeps the TIFFs small.
# wider canvas so the figure fills the page width (panels scale to fit).
comp.width<-34
comp.height<-32
comp.dpi<-300

# enlarged text styling for the composite panels (bigger for publication / Word). These are
# shared across full-tree and subtree panels; column-name size/offset are set per call below
# (doubled relative to each context's standalone size). Standalone plots are unaffected.
cp.style<-list(
  legend.text.size   = 14 * 1.5,   # +50%
  legend.title.size  = 16 * 1.5,   # +50%
  legend.title.face  = "bold",     # bold legend titles
  seg.label.size     = 11 * 1.25,  # +25%
  n.label.size       = 5  * 1.25,  # +25%
  treescale.fontsize = 6,          # scale-bar text (was 3)
  treescale.gap.frac = 0.05,       # gap between scale bar and its label (fraction of Ntip)
  treescale.width    = 0.05,       # all scale bars show 0.05 -- fine for full trees only
  treescale.right    = TRUE        # top-right of the tree, right-aligned at rel x = 1
)

# genotype-MRCA subtree panels are much shallower than full trees (root-to-tip depth on
# the order of 0.003-0.04 subs/site vs 0.05 for cp.style's fixed bar width), so a
# right-aligned 0.05-wide bar routinely lands at a NEGATIVE x position, forcing ggplot to
# expand the x-axis to fit it and squashing the actual tree into a sliver of the panel.
# Same style as cp.style but a bar small enough to fit every subtree, and top-left instead
# of top-right. xfrac=0.25 (not label.xfrac's 0.05) -- tested directly against label.xfrac,
# which collides with the bold seg.label/n= text sitting right at x_range*0.05.
cp.style.subtree<-modifyList(cp.style, list(
  treescale.width = 0.005, treescale.right = FALSE, treescale.xfrac = 0.25
))

# placeholder for a segment/genotype combo that has too few tips to plot
blank_panel<-function(lab){
  ggdraw() + draw_label(lab, fontface = "italic", size = 22, colour = "grey40")
}

# arrange a named list of panel objects into a 2x2 grid (filling missing panels)
assemble_grid<-function(objs, segs){
  pl<-lapply(segs, function(s){
    o<-objs[[s]]
    if(is.null(o)) blank_panel(paste0(s, ": n/a")) else o
  })
  plot_grid(plotlist = pl, ncol = 2)
}

save_composite<-function(grid, file){
  ggsave(file, plot = grid, width = comp.width, height = comp.height,
         units = "in", dpi = comp.dpi, compression = "lzw", limitsize = FALSE)
  cat("wrote", file, "\n")
}

# build per-segment panels once, reused across both groups and (for full trees) saved
full_objs<-list()
gf_objs<-setNames(vector("list", length(genoflu_top)), genoflu_top)  # gf_objs[[g]][[seg]]
gi_objs<-setNames(vector("list", length(genin_top)),   genin_top)

for(seg in segments){
  bundle<-build_anno(seg, geno)
  tree<-bundle$tree
  anno<-bundle$anno

  cl_pals<-build_cluster_palettes(anno)
  specs<-base_specs(palettes, cl_pals)
  specs_genoflu<-Filter(function(s) !s$col %in% c("genin_cluster","genin_geno"), specs)
  specs_genin  <-Filter(function(s) !s$col %in% c("geno_cluster","genoflu_geno"), specs)

  # full-tree panel (no per-segment file; the main run loop already wrote those).
  # HA adds the H5-clade column (leftmost); NA adds the subtype column, matching the
  # *_full_gheatmap_H5clade / _subtype variants.
  full_specs<-specs
  if(seg=="HA") full_specs<-c(list(clade_spec(palettes)), specs)
  if(seg=="NA") full_specs<-c(list(subtype_spec(palettes)), specs)
  # widen full-tree legends to 4 columns so the stacked legend box is shorter and does not
  # get cut off in the composites; tc_geno stays ncol=1 (whole-genome strings too long).
  full_specs<-lapply(full_specs, function(s){if(s$col!="tc_geno") s$ncol<-4; s})
  # column names enlarged (4 -> 7.2) and shifted further off the columns (1.5 -> 3)
  full_objs[[seg]]<-do.call(make_plot, c(
    list(tree, anno, full_specs, file = NULL, seg.label = seg, legend.key.cm = 0.65,
         font.size = 7.2, colnames_offset_y = 3), cp.style))

  # genotype-MRCA subtree panels (returned, not written); column names enlarged (5 -> 9)
  # and shifted further off the columns (1 -> 2)
  for(g in genoflu_top){
    gf_objs[[g]][[seg]]<-do.call(plot_subtree, c(
      list(tree, anno, specs_genoflu, "genoflu_geno", g, file = NULL, seg.label = seg,
           font.size = 9, colnames_offset_y = 2), cp.style.subtree))
  }
  for(g in genin_top){
    gi_objs[[g]][[seg]]<-do.call(plot_subtree, c(
      list(tree, anno, specs_genin, "genin_geno", g, file = NULL, seg.label = seg,
           font.size = 9, colnames_offset_y = 2), cp.style.subtree))
  }
}

# full-tree composites
comp.out<-paste0(f.out, "composites/")
if(!dir.exists(comp.out)){dir.create(comp.out)}
for(gn in names(comp_groups)){
  save_composite(assemble_grid(full_objs, comp_groups[[gn]]),
                 paste0(comp.out, "composite_full_", gn, ".tiff"))
}

# genotype composites -> into each genotype's folder
for(g in genoflu_top){
  for(gn in names(comp_groups)){
    save_composite(assemble_grid(gf_objs[[g]], comp_groups[[gn]]),
                   paste0(geno_dir("genoflu", g), "composite_plot_geno_", gn, ".tiff"))
  }
}
for(g in genin_top){
  for(gn in names(comp_groups)){
    save_composite(assemble_grid(gi_objs[[g]], comp_groups[[gn]]),
                   paste0(geno_dir("genin", g), "composite_plot_geno_", gn, ".tiff"))
  }
}
```

# All-8-segment composites (single figure)
One figure with all 8 segments in standard IAV order (PB2, PB1, PA, HA, NP, NA, M, NS),
4 columns x 2 rows, left-to-right / top-to-bottom. Exported at double the width of the 2x2
composites above. Reuses the panel objects (`full_objs` / `gf_objs` / `gi_objs`) built in the
previous chunk, so run that chunk first.
```{r}
if(!exists("full_objs")){
  stop("Run the 'Publication composites (cowplot)' chunk first to build the panel objects.")
}

seg_order8<-c("PB2","PB1","PA","HA","NP","NA","M","NS")  # standard IAV order
comp8.width<-comp.width * 2   # double width vs the 2x2 composites
comp8.height<-comp.height
comp8.ncol<-4

assemble_grid8<-function(objs){
  pl<-lapply(seg_order8, function(s){
    o<-objs[[s]]
    if(is.null(o)) blank_panel(paste0(s, ": n/a")) else o
  })
  plot_grid(plotlist = pl, ncol = comp8.ncol)
}

save_composite8<-function(grid, file){
  ggsave(file, plot = grid, width = comp8.width, height = comp8.height,
         units = "in", dpi = comp.dpi, compression = "lzw", limitsize = FALSE)
  cat("wrote", file, "\n")
}

# full tree, all 8 segments
save_composite8(assemble_grid8(full_objs),
                paste0(comp.out, "composite_full_all8.tiff"))

# genotype trees, all 8 segments -> into each genotype's folder
for(g in genoflu_top){
  save_composite8(assemble_grid8(gf_objs[[g]]),
                  paste0(geno_dir("genoflu", g), "composite_plot_geno_all8.tiff"))
}
for(g in genin_top){
  save_composite8(assemble_grid8(gi_objs[[g]]),
                  paste0(geno_dir("genin", g), "composite_plot_geno_all8.tiff"))
}
```

# High-resolution full-tree composites (TIFF + PNG)
Re-exports the full-tree composites (both 2x2 groups + all-8) at `hires.dpi` as both TIFF and
PNG, same canvas size as above, so only pixel density changes. Written to `composites/` with
a `_<dpi>dpi` suffix. Uses ragg devices, which cope with very large rasters (the base png device
can fail at these sizes). Reuses `full_objs`, so run the 'Publication composites' chunk first.
The all-8 figure uses `hires8.dpi` (450) because its canvas is too large for ragg at 600 dpi.
```{r}
if(!exists("full_objs")){
  stop("Run the 'Publication composites (cowplot)' chunk first to build the panel objects.")
}

hires.dpi<-600
# ragg caps a raster at ~2^31 bytes (~536M px RGBA). The all-8 canvas (68 x 32 in) exceeds that
# at 600 dpi (783M px), so it gets its own lower dpi: 450 -> 30600 x 14400 px (~441M px).
hires8.dpi<-450

save_hires<-function(grid, file.stem, width, height, dpi = hires.dpi){
  ggsave(paste0(file.stem, "_", dpi, "dpi.tiff"), plot = grid, device = ragg::agg_tiff,
         width = width, height = height, units = "in", dpi = dpi,
         compression = "lzw", limitsize = FALSE)
  ggsave(paste0(file.stem, "_", dpi, "dpi.png"), plot = grid, device = ragg::agg_png,
         width = width, height = height, units = "in", dpi = dpi, limitsize = FALSE)
  cat("wrote", file.stem, "(tiff + png) at", dpi, "dpi\n")
}

for(gn in names(comp_groups)){
  save_hires(assemble_grid(full_objs, comp_groups[[gn]]),
             paste0(comp.out, "composite_full_", gn), comp.width, comp.height)
}
save_hires(assemble_grid8(full_objs),
           paste0(comp.out, "composite_full_all8"), comp8.width, comp8.height, dpi = hires8.dpi)
```
